The page directly maps Jamie's work to delivery coordination, risk visibility, decision systems, stakeholder dependencies, adoption materials, and durable operating documentation.
The case study separates Jamie's documented project role from the later municipal sequence and explicitly declines to claim an executed agreement, disbursement, receipt, expenditure, or construction.
Nine accessible same-page references include numerical markers, meaningful labels, local targets, and backlinks while preserving CallNYC's archived, independent, and unofficial status.

The grouped work index and repeated unclear-to-usable framing are highly scannable, though the similarly structured cards and extensive boundary sections make deeper portfolio review somewhat repetitive.

Jamie is visible as co-founder and builder of campaign websites, source maps, coordination records, and public guidance, with collective campaign credit preserved; some operating-language density still requires careful reading.
Artifact-gallery cards describe the work but do not show approved screenshots, documents, interfaces, photographs, or other primary visual artifacts.
The HTML summary and approved PDF reinforce the same technical-project-management positioning, project chronology, CouncilStat attribution, quantified achievements, and contact path.

Candidate-bound browser evidence shows no overflow across ten desktop, mobile, and 200-percent-equivalent views, with visible focus on all 24 traversed controls; the zoom result is standards-equivalent reflow rather than direct browser-chrome zoom.
Canonical metadata, Open Graph title and image, Twitter card, working resume download, and direct contact links are present; final production-domain verification is appropriately deferred.
Repository, safety, citation, route, resume, and responsive checks pass, but deployed production SHA, smoke, rollback, indexing, and human-approval evidence are production-only deferrals.
